# Sync

Locks, conditions, once-only initialization, semaphores, barriers, wait groups and channels for threads.

## Installation

Add `Sync` to the `[Dependencies]` table of your package's `Rux.toml`:

```toml
[Dependencies]
Sync = { Namespace = "Rux", Version = "0.1.0" }
```

Standard packages are declared by hand: the registry does not serve them, so `rux add Rux/Sync` cannot add them.

## Dependencies

- [`Core`](/docs/api/core) 0.1.0
- [`FreeBSD`](/docs/api/freebsd) 0.1.0 (FreeBSD only)
- [`Linux`](/docs/api/linux) 0.1.0 (Linux only)
- [`macOS`](/docs/api/macos) 0.1.0 (macOS only)
- [`Memory`](/docs/api/memory) 0.1.0
- [`Time`](/docs/api/time) 0.1.0
- [`Windows`](/docs/api/windows) 0.1.0 (Windows only)

## Guide

### What it provides

| Module                                      | Covers                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Lock`                                      | `Lock`, a bare lock, and [`Once`](/docs/api/sync/lock#once), a once-only initialization; both can be module variables                                                                        |
| [`Mutex`](/docs/api/sync/mutex#mutex)       | [`Mutex<T>`](/docs/api/sync/mutex#mutex) with its [`MutexGuard<T>`](/docs/api/sync/mutex#mutex-guard), and [`Condition`](/docs/api/sync/mutex#condition) to wait on while holding one        |
| [`RwLock`](/docs/api/sync/rw-lock#rw-lock)  | [`RwLock<T>`](/docs/api/sync/rw-lock#rw-lock) with [`ReadGuard<T>`](/docs/api/sync/rw-lock#read-guard) and [`WriteGuard<T>`](/docs/api/sync/rw-lock#write-guard): many readers or one writer |
| `Counters`                                  | [`Semaphore`](/docs/api/sync/counters#semaphore), [`Barrier`](/docs/api/sync/counters#barrier) and [`WaitGroup`](/docs/api/sync/counters#wait-group)                                         |
| [`Channel`](/docs/api/sync/channel#channel) | [`Channel<T>`](/docs/api/sync/channel#channel), a bounded queue any number of threads send to and receive from                                                                               |

The module names describe where each declaration comes from; they are not part of an import path.

### Example

```rux
import Sync::Mutex;
import Thread::{ JoinHandle, Spawn };

func AddOne(total: Mutex<uint64>) -> () {
    let guard = total.Lock();
    *guard.Get() = *guard.Get() + 1u64;
}

func Main() -> int {
    let total = Mutex<uint64>(0u64);
    var first = Spawn(AddOne, total.Clone()) catch { else => return 1 };
    var second = Spawn(AddOne, total.Clone()) catch { else => return 1 };
    first.Join();
    second.Join();
    let guard = total.Lock();
    return *guard.Get() == 2u64 ? 0 : 2;
}
```

### Design

Every type here waits the same way: a thread sleeps on a 32-bit word only while the word still holds the value it last saw, and the system checks that as it puts the thread to sleep, so a change that lands just before the sleep is never missed. That is `futex` on Linux, `_umtx_op` on FreeBSD, `__ulock_wait` on macOS and `WaitOnAddress` on Windows. Taking a free lock and releasing one nobody waits for are each one atomic instruction; only contention costs a system call.

`Lock` and [`Once`](/docs/api/sync/lock#once) live where they are declared and need no destroying, so a module variable can be one, starting as [`Lock::Unlocked`](/docs/api/sync/lock#unlocked) or [`Once::Incomplete`](/docs/api/sync/lock#incomplete), and every thread names it directly. The other types are handles to storage their clones share: `Clone` gives another handle to move to another thread, and the storage, with the value a [`Mutex<T>`](/docs/api/sync/mutex#mutex), [`RwLock<T>`](/docs/api/sync/rw-lock#rw-lock) or [`Channel<T>`](/docs/api/sync/channel#channel) holds, is destroyed when the last handle and the last guard are gone. A guard is the only way to reach a guarded value, and it releases its lock when it is dropped. The value's address a guard hands out is valid only while the guard holds the lock.

None of the locks is reentrant, and none queues its waiters in order: [`RwLock`](/docs/api/sync/rw-lock#rw-lock) can keep a writer waiting behind a steady stream of readers. A [`Condition`](/docs/api/sync/mutex#condition) wait can return without a notification, so it is always written in a loop that checks the condition. Running out of memory while creating one of these objects is a program error, as is misuse the type cannot recover from, such as marking a [`WaitGroup`](/docs/api/sync/counters#wait-group) done more times than work was added.

## Index

### Types

| Name                                                  | Summary                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [`Channel<T>`](/docs/api/sync/channel#channel)        | A bounded queue of values passed between threads, any number of which may send and receive.                                                                        |
| [`Semaphore`](/docs/api/sync/counters#semaphore)      | A count of permits that threads take and give back, waiting while none is left.                                                                                    |
| [`Barrier`](/docs/api/sync/counters#barrier)          | A meeting point a fixed number of threads wait at until all of them have arrived, then pass together.                                                              |
| [`WaitGroup`](/docs/api/sync/counters#wait-group)     | A count of unfinished work that threads add to and mark done, and that others wait to see reach zero.                                                              |
| [`Lock`](/docs/api/sync/lock#lock)                    | A lock that guards nothing in particular: whatever the code between [`Acquire`](/docs/api/sync/lock#acquire) and [`Release`](/docs/api/sync/lock#release) touches. |
| [`Once`](/docs/api/sync/lock#once)                    | Runs one initialization once, however many threads ask for it at once.                                                                                             |
| [`Mutex<T>`](/docs/api/sync/mutex#mutex)              | A value guarded by a lock, shared between the threads that hold a handle to it.                                                                                    |
| [`MutexGuard<T>`](/docs/api/sync/mutex#mutex-guard)   | The lock on a [`Mutex<T>`](/docs/api/sync/mutex#mutex), held for as long as the guard lives, and the way to reach the value.                                       |
| [`Condition`](/docs/api/sync/mutex#condition)         | A condition threads wait on while holding a [`Mutex<T>`](/docs/api/sync/mutex#mutex), until another thread says it may hold.                                       |
| [`RwLock<T>`](/docs/api/sync/rw-lock#rw-lock)         | A value guarded by a lock that many readers or one writer may hold, shared between the threads that hold a handle.                                                 |
| [`ReadGuard<T>`](/docs/api/sync/rw-lock#read-guard)   | A shared hold on an [`RwLock<T>`](/docs/api/sync/rw-lock#rw-lock): the value may be read, and other readers may hold it too.                                       |
| [`WriteGuard<T>`](/docs/api/sync/rw-lock#write-guard) | The exclusive hold on an [`RwLock<T>`](/docs/api/sync/rw-lock#rw-lock): the value may be read and written, and nobody else holds the lock.                         |
